quotes.text: It's a managed service that sits between your back-end APIs and the apps, websites, devices, and partners that consume them. But here's the thing. It's not just a proxy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Plain-English definition of Azure API Management.

quotes.text: One more thing, the gateway hides your real backend URL. Clients only see the gateway address. Your backend servers stay hidden from the internet.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains a key security benefit of the gateway.

quotes.text: The key takeaway is this, policies let you control how your API's behave without touching the code that runs them. That means faster changes, fewer deployments, and less risk.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes why policies are the engine of APIM.

quotes.text: This layered approach builds defense in depth, authentication at the gateway, secrets in a vault, network isolation around your back ends. Each layer strengthens the next.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Start with developer for testing. Move to standard for production. Go premium if you need global scale or private networking.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

chapters.title: Why many APIs turn into chaos
The problem: too many APIs, no control
What Azure API Management is: gateway, management plane, developer portal
The gateway, your API's front door
Policies, the engine that controls everything

takeaways: Azure API Management is a managed service in front of your backend APIs that covers their full lifecycle through a gateway, a management plane and a developer portal.

Policies let you add authentication, rate limiting, caching and transformations at the gateway without changing backend code, while products and subscription keys package APIs for different consumers.

For production, combine OAuth 2.0 with Entra ID, Key Vault-backed named values, managed identities and network isolation, and pick the tier from developer for testing to standard or premium for production.
hook: As applications split into dozens of microservices, every team ends up reinventing authentication, logging and rate limiting, and nobody has a single view of API traffic. This Simply Explained episode is for developers, architects and Azure admins who want to understand Azure API Management in plain English: the gateway, policies, products, the developer portal, security and pricing tiers.
